phases.evidence: Repository metadata, public claims, examples, canonical CLI smoke checks, and native execution of the Sotlas-written lexer subset, including keyword classification and source spans.
phases.boundary: Documentation and acceptance claims; lexer execution is not a stage1/stage2 self-hosting proof and does not certify every language feature.

phases.evidence: Canonical check pipeline and typed AST semantic cases.
phases.boundary: Most semantic cases are checker tests; native execution is limited to explicit fixtures.

phases.evidence: Canonical ownership/SIR placement, static rejection, legacy native probes, and production C11 execution of the supported region, direct, whisper, ISLAND-to-EXCLUSIVE handover, and repr(C) external-wrapper subsets. Native caller probes check destructor counts and transferred field values.
phases.boundary: The supported structured subset is tested; arbitrary CFG and full runtime ARC remain outside the contract.

phases.evidence: Canonical authority checks, typed SIR facts, and ABI contract validation.
phases.boundary: Reference ABI tests do not imply vendor GPU/NPU execution.

phases.evidence: Canonical state typing and transition validation.
phases.boundary: Only declared state-transition forms are accepted.

phases.evidence: Effect inference and backend rejection contracts.
phases.boundary: Effect checking does not sandbox external side effects.

phases.evidence: Canonical typed plans/SIR; the reference CPU runner interprets pure integer/boolean stages and schedules independent layers with error/cancellation propagation. C11 entrypoints execute pure scalar integer, f32/f64, and bool graphs in deterministic dependency order, including graphs with independent stages. C and Sotlas callers can invoke the generated entrypoint through its checked C ABI declaration.
phases.boundary: The reference interpreter and native backend cover different instruction/type subsets; native signed overflow is not defined by the language. C11 uses a serial fallback and does not promise parallel speedup. Source calls require the exact generated symbol and an @system function; there is no dedicated Flow invocation syntax. Native callers receive only the final stage result. Ownership payloads and GPU/NPU dispatch remain unsupported.

phases.evidence: Target normalization, feature contracts, and LLVM emission checks.
phases.boundary: This is not a complete platform ABI or a Sotlas machine-code backend.

phases.evidence: Checked DEVICE lifecycle and reference C11 provider integration, including invalid arguments, output preservation, capacity exhaustion, and lifecycle sequencing.
phases.boundary: No physical GPU/NPU, vendor driver, DMA, or hardware completion is implemented.

phases.evidence: Foreign boundary classification, explicit unsafe checks, and fail-closed validation.
phases.boundary: Trust labels do not create process isolation or a sandbox.

phases.evidence: Supported preconditions, refinements, and deterministic reports.
phases.boundary: Only the documented predicate subset is proved.

phases.evidence: Source and checked Flow call/dependency explanations.
phases.boundary: Ambiguous mutation and unresolved control flow remain fail-closed.

phases.evidence: Certified graph recovery and selected pure SIR equivalence cases.
phases.boundary: Proof is limited to the tested normalization and scalar subset.

phases.evidence: Effect policy checks and sequential compensation behavior.
phases.boundary: Parallel transactional execution and arbitrary rollback semantics are rejected.

phases.evidence: Selection among checked eligible Flow alternatives, fallback reports, and explicit provider availability requirements.
phases.boundary: Provider availability is supplied by the caller; intent does not discover or dispatch physical hardware.

phases.evidence: Canonical SIR facts, validation, and reports.
phases.boundary: SIR body lowering remains a certified subset, not complete lowering for the language.

phases.evidence: Direct LLVM subset emission, native execution, and C11/LLVM differential checks for unsigned parameter/literal arithmetic and signed comparison inputs.
phases.boundary: Parity covers only tested forms. LLVM provides target code generation; Sotlas does not yet own register allocation or a machine backend.
Reports describe only facts represented by the checked subset.
